subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 9: Literacy – Writing an informal email
outcomes: Choose a good subject line for an email.
Start and finish an informal email correctly.
Use unless (= if not) and answer all the writer's questions.

tf.s: The subject line tells the reader why you are writing.
tf.why: Yes, the subject explains the reason.

tf.s: We start an informal email with 'Dear Sir'.
tf.why: Informal emails start with Hi + name.

tf.s: We can finish an informal email with 'See you soon' + your name.
The best subject line for Kamla's email is 'Next weekend!'.
tf.why: Well done, it explains why she is writing.

tf.s: Kamla needs to buy a present for her father.
tf.why: Kamla needs a present for her mother.

tf.s: In a reply, you only need to answer one of the writer's questions.
tf.why: Answer all of the writer's questions.

tf.s: 'Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus' means 'If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus'.
tf.why: Yes, both sentences mean the same.
Paragraphs make an email easy to read.

tf.s: 'I won't go unless it doesn't stop raining' is correct.
tf.why: Unless already means 'if not': I won't go unless it stops raining.

boxes.q: How do we start an informal email?
boxes.why: Informal emails begin with Hi + name.

boxes.q: How do we finish an informal email?
boxes.why: Friendly endings: Bye or See you soon.

boxes.q: What goes in the subject box?
boxes.why: The subject tells the reason for writing.

boxes.q: What does Kamla need to buy?
boxes.why: Kamla needs a present for her mother.

boxes.q: Rewrite: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
o: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the bus.
Unless you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.
If you hurry, you'll miss the bus.

boxes.q: Who writes the reply to Kamla?
What is the best subject line for Kamla's email?
boxes.why: 'Next weekend!' tells why she is writing.

boxes.q: Zainab must write about the shops where she lives, her favourite shop and ...
o: what else there is to do there

boxes.q: Rewrite: I won't go if it doesn't stop raining.
o: I won't go unless it stops raining.
I won't go unless it doesn't stop raining.
I go unless it rains not.

mcq.q: What does an informal email start with?
mcq.why: Hi + name is friendly and informal.

mcq.q: What does the subject line explain?
mcq.why: The subject tells the reader the reason.

mcq.q: What should you do when you plan a reply?
o: make sure you answer all of the writer's questions
mcq.why: A good plan answers every question.

mcq.q: Rewrite with unless: I won't have time to get it if I don't go next weekend.
o: I won't have time to get it unless I go next weekend.
I won't have time to get it unless I don't go next weekend.
I will have time unless I go.
Unless I won't go, I have time.

mcq.q: Which is the best last line of an informal email?
mcq.why: Finish with See you soon or Bye + your name.

o: Unless it stops raining, we won't go out.
Unless it doesn't stop raining, we won't go out.
Unless it will stop raining, we go out.
Unless stop raining, we won't go.

mcq.q: Why is 'Next weekend!' a better subject line than 'Hello'?
o: It tells the reader why Kamla is writing.
mcq.why: A good subject explains the reason for the email.

mcq.q: Zainab's reply only talks about her favourite shop. What is the problem?
o: She hasn't answered all of Kamla's questions.
mcq.why: A good reply answers all the questions.

o: Hi Kamla, I'd love to see you next weekend! See you soon, Zainab
Dear Sir, I am writing to complain. Yours faithfully
To the manager: Please send the bill.
Dear Madam, Thank you for your letter.
mcq.why: It uses Hi, friendly words and See you soon.
